The experimental coverage is substantial, including multiple MIM frameworks, backbone sizes, downstream datasets, and other pretraining paradigms. Reported ImageNet gains over linear probing are considerable: 67.7% to 75.6% for MAE and 51.5% to 65.1% for SimMIM.

The projection, query-count, and dimensionality ablations are useful. Additional low-data and intermediate-layer experiments strengthen the evidence that attentive aggregation accesses information missed by linear probing.
weaknesses: The methodological novelty is limited, and a decisive efficiency control is missing. Equation (10) is an exact reparameterization of Equation (7). Existing learned-query MHCA can evaluate X^T(W_Kj^T q_j) without projecting every token; Equation (2) likewise permits value projection after pooling. Comparing against these algebraically optimized implementations is necessary to establish how much computational advantage comes specifically from EP.

The headline '10× speed-up over conventional multi-head attention' is not demonstrated. Section 4.3 compares 0.12 versus 1.44 GFLOPs against a full ViT block, while Figure 4 shows much smaller differences against attentive probes such as AIM. These are probe-only operation counts, with no measured latency, training throughput, or peak memory. They do not establish the claimed practical speed-up.

Baseline fidelity needs verification. Appendix B.1 describes CLIP pooling and CaiT class attention as full-token self-attention, although their global output can be computed using only the global query. Counting unused token outputs can inflate baseline computation and compromise the central efficiency comparison.

The comparison protocol does not convincingly establish optimal trade-offs. Appendix C.4 fixes LARS and learning rate 0.1 on ImageNet and Places365 without method-specific tuning, while EP receives extensive query-count and output-dimension sweeps. Figure 7 partially addresses baseline capacity tuning on one setting, but no repeated-run uncertainty is reported for relatively small advantages over strong attentive baselines.

Reproducibility and performance claims need tightening. The manuscript lacks a code link and complete per-experiment configurations, including query initialization, attention scaling, checkpoint identifiers, and selected EP settings. Moreover, Figures 3 and 9 show existing methods exceeding EP's accuracy in several settings, including SimMIM and MAE ViT-S. The evidence supports favorable trade-offs, rather than the abstract's broad claim of outperforming prior attentive approaches across benchmarks.

The localization analysis does not establish robustness or avoidance of background shortcuts. Correlations between attention concentration, bounding-box mass, and uniform-replacement accuracy drops are informative but not causal evidence. Globally contextualized patch tokens can encode background information even when attention falls inside an object. Background interventions and quantitative query-diversity measurements would be needed to support the stronger interpretability claims.

An existing fixed-query MHCA implementation can compute these effective queries before multiplying by image features. Comparing against this algebraically optimized baseline is essential to separate the benefits of the proposed training parameterization from avoidable computation in baseline implementations.

The central claim of up to 10× speed-up is not established by the reported measurements. Section 4.3 obtains its large ratio from 0.12 versus 1.44 GFLOPs using a full ViT block as the comparator; the attentive baselines in Figure 4 are substantially closer. FLOP reductions do not establish runtime speed-ups, and no training throughput, latency, peak-memory, or end-to-end measurements including the backbone are reported.

Baseline definitions raise additional concerns about the efficiency benchmark. Appendix B describes CLIP and CaiT pooling as full self-attention. For a single attention layer whose retained output is only the pooled/class token, only that token's query needs to be evaluated. Computing discarded patch-query outputs adds unnecessary work and can inflate the reported baseline cost.

The evaluation protocol does not sufficiently establish reliable comparative rankings. Appendix C.4 fixes the learning rate to 0.1 for all methods on ImageNet and Places365 despite their different parameterizations. The paper reports no repeated-run uncertainty and does not clearly specify a separate hyperparameter-selection split. Code, exact checkpoint identifiers, and several optimizer and initialization details are also absent, limiting reproducibility.

The claim of outperforming prior attentive approaches across benchmarks is stronger than the results support. EP often offers a favorable parameter trade-off, but competitors achieve higher absolute accuracy in several settings, including SimMIM in Figure 3 and Aircraft, Places365, and SUN397 in Figure 9. The abstract should distinguish parameter efficiency from accuracy superiority.

The localization analysis supports an association, not the claims that EP avoids shortcuts or improves robustness. Replacing attention with uniform weights perturbs low-entropy maps more strongly, which can itself explain part of the relationship with accuracy loss. Bounding-box attention mass and selected visualizations do not establish causal foreground reliance, robustness to background changes, or consistently nonredundant query specialization.

weaknesses: The methodological novelty is modest. For the fixed-query MHCA formulation, EP is an exact head-wise reparameterization using u_j = W_Kj^T q_j. This is a useful simplification, but the main contribution consequently depends on the rigor of the empirical benchmark. Section 4.3 also conflates absorbing the key projection with setting it to identity, which instead restricts queries to channel subsets.

The computational comparisons omit straightforward equivalent implementations. Computing W_Kj^T q_j before multiplying by patch features avoids the baseline's per-patch key projection. Appendix B also describes full-token self-attention for CLIP/CaiT although only the global-token output is retained; unnecessary query outputs can be omitted. Comparisons against these optimized implementations are needed to establish the claimed computational advantage.

Practical efficiency remains insufficiently demonstrated. Despite claims of substantial compute and memory gains, there are no measured training times, inference throughput, or peak-memory results. Figure 3 explicitly excludes the 17.58-GFLOP backbone, which dominates the reported forward computation; large reductions in probe-only FLOPs therefore do not establish comparable overall savings.

The benchmark lacks important experimental controls. Appendix C.1 fixes the learning rate to 0.1 on ImageNet and Places365, without demonstrating that the different probe architectures are comparably optimized. No repeated-run uncertainty is reported, despite several small performance differences. Optimizer exceptions, checkpoint identifiers, initialization, and other training details are insufficiently specified for reliable reproduction.

Several claims exceed the comparisons provided. EP does not consistently achieve the highest accuracy across seven benchmarks: on Places365, for example, EP reaches 53.7% versus 54.84% for the ViT probe. Its strongest demonstrated advantage is the parameter trade-off. Moreover, the broad pre-training comparison and limited-label experiments omit competing attentive probes, so they do not establish that those gains are specific to EP.

The attention analysis does not substantiate claims about avoiding shortcuts or improving robustness. Replacing attention with uniform weights perturbs concentrated distributions more strongly by construction, confounding the entropy–accuracy-drop relationship. Bounding-box attention mass and complementary maps also do not establish causal reliance on object parts, especially with contextualized ViT tokens. Background interventions or robustness evaluations are needed for the stronger conclusions.

The blanket ten-epoch convergence claim also conflicts with Table 9: MAE achieves 60.0% at ten epochs versus 67.7% for linear probing and 75.6% for fully trained EP.

Reproducibility is incomplete despite the extensive experiments. The manuscript provides no code link and omits consequential details such as query initialization, weight decay, learning-rate decay, optimizer exceptions, and diffusion-model feature extraction settings.

strengths: The core reparameterization is mathematically sound and practically simple. Absorbing the learned query and key projection preserves the attention function while reducing parameters. Section 4.3 reports identical 75.1% accuracy for matched EP and AIM configurations, with 1.36M versus 1.95M trainable parameters.
The empirical coverage is substantial: seven classification datasets, multiple backbone sizes, diverse pre-training paradigms, and numerous attentive-pooling and PEFT baselines.
The improvements over linear probing are meaningful, particularly for patch-oriented representations: ImageNet accuracy increases from 67.7% to 75.6% for MAE ViT-B and from 51.5% to 65.1% for SimMIM.

The projection, query-count, and dimensionality ablations help explain the design. Low-shot experiments, cross-dataset transfer, and the successful LoRA+EP combination provide additional evidence of practical utility.
weaknesses: Methodological novelty is modest. EP is principally an algebraic reparameterization of existing fixed-query cross-attention, with dimensionality reduction providing another efficiency control. The contribution therefore depends heavily on the rigor of the benchmark and the demonstrated practical savings.

The accuracy–parameter comparisons need stronger controls. Appendix C.1 fixes the learning rate to 0.1 on ImageNet and Places365 despite comparing substantially different parameterizations. EP receives extensive query-count and output-dimension sweeps; Figure 15 partially addresses this for AIM, but comparable bottleneck-classifier sweeps for linear probing and LoRA are missing. These omissions weaken claims of Pareto dominance.

Baseline fidelity requires clarification. Appendix B describes CLIP attention pooling and CaiT class attention as full token self-attention, whereas their standard pooling formulations require queries only from the pooled/class token. Computing unnecessary token outputs can inflate their FLOPs without changing the relevant output. The implementations and computational comparisons should be reconciled with the original methods.

The evidence for practical computational and memory efficiency is incomplete. Figure 3 explicitly measures probe-head FLOPs, while the actual training protocol repeatedly executes the 17.58-GFLOP backbone. No end-to-end timing or peak-memory measurements are provided. Existing fixed-query MHCA can also precompute its effective queries at inference, which deserves an optimized comparison.

Reproducibility and statistical support are insufficient for the smaller claimed gains. Results lack variation across training seeds, and the hyperparameter-selection split, query initialization, weight decay, and optimizer exceptions are not adequately specified. These details matter when comparing equivalent functions trained under different parameterizations.

Several interpretations exceed the evidence. Foreground attention and complementary maps do not establish robustness or avoidance of background shortcuts; replacing attention with uniform also perturbs sharper distributions more strongly, confounding the entropy analysis. Localization trained with image labels should be described as weakly supervised. The convergence claim also needs qualification: Table 9 reports MAE EP@10 at 60.0%, below LP@90 at 67.7%.

strengths: Addresses an important evaluation problem: linear probing can underestimate representations whose useful information is distributed across patch tokens. The comparison across seven datasets and diverse pre-training paradigms is a substantial empirical contribution.

The key-query absorption underlying EP is mathematically sound for fixed learned queries. The matched-head comparison provides concrete evidence: EP12 and AIM12 both achieve 75.1% accuracy, while EP reduces trainable parameters from 1.95M to 1.36M.

The accuracy–parameter trade-offs are promising. On ImageNet-1K, EP improves MAE ViT-B from 67.7% to 75.6% and SimMIM from 51.5% to 65.1%. Ablations examine query count, output dimensionality, and projection matrices.

The appendix provides useful additional evidence through limited-label classification, cross-dataset evaluation, retrieval, and LoRA combinations. The reported hybrid result of 76.99% with approximately 850K parameters supports EP’s practical usefulness beyond standalone probing.
weaknesses: The methodological novelty is limited. Equation (10) is an algebraic reparameterization of existing learned-query attention, rather than a more expressive attention mechanism. Matched-head results demonstrate retained accuracy with fewer training parameters, but do not establish a fundamentally new aggregation capability. The paper’s strongest contribution is therefore the empirical study, whose comparative rigor becomes especially important.

Baseline optimization is insufficiently controlled for the strongest superiority claims. Appendix C.1 fixes the learning rate at 0.1 on ImageNet-1K and Places365 and mostly uses LARS, without establishing that this configuration is appropriate across substantially different probe architectures and PEFT methods. EP receives extensive configuration sweeps, while most competing probes receive narrower exploration. Table 2 also uses GAP for SigLIP-family models; comparisons against their native frozen attentive readouts would better establish the gains over standard feature extraction.

The computational advantage needs stronger validation. Existing learned-query MHCA can evaluate Equation (7) as X^T(W_K^T q), avoiding an explicit key projection for every patch; its fixed query and key parameters can also be folded at inference. Appendix B’s full self-attention implementations of CLIP/CaiT warrant comparison with implementations computing only the required pooled query. Moreover, Figure 3 excludes the unchanged 17.58-GFLOP backbone, and no measured training time or peak memory is provided. The trainable-parameter savings are convincing, but substantial practical compute and memory savings remain insufficiently demonstrated.

Statistical reliability and reproducibility are incomplete. Results lack repeated-run variability or confidence intervals, which matters for small improvements over strong attentive baselines. The manuscript also omits details such as query initialization, the complete optimization configuration, and sufficiently explicit PEFT training settings.

The interpretation of attention maps exceeds the evidence. Replacing a concentrated distribution with uniform attention creates a larger perturbation than replacing an already diffuse distribution, confounding the entropy-versus-accuracy-drop analysis. Foreground attention and complementarity do not establish avoidance of background shortcuts or consistent semantic-part correspondence. Controlled background interventions and quantitative part annotations would strengthen these claims. Table 6’s localization setting also uses an image-label-trained probe and should be described as weakly supervised.

Several general statements need qualification. EP does not achieve the highest accuracy throughout Figure 9, and Table 8 shows BEiTv2 retrieval R@1 decreasing from 48.3 to 44.2. The rapid-convergence discussion overlooks MAE’s 60.0% accuracy after 10 epochs versus 67.7% for completed linear probing. These exceptions should be reflected in the claims of consistent superiority and near-optimal early convergence.

Most competitors receive less extensive architectural exploration than EP, although AIM is partially ablated. These choices leave uncertainty about the claimed Pareto frontiers.

Additionally, Appendix B treats CLIP/CaiT pooling as full self-attention, although their retained global-token output can be computed using only its query. Comparative tuning is insufficiently established. Appendix C.1 fixes the learning rate at 0.1 on ImageNet and Places365 while mostly using LARS across heterogeneous methods. EP receives extensive query-count and output-dimension sweeps. Figure 15 partially addresses AIM, but similarly compressed linear and LoRA classifiers are missing, leaving some low-parameter advantages confounded with classifier dimensionality.

Appendix B describes CLIP and CaiT pooling as full self-attention over all tokens, although their standard pooling/class-attention stages only require the global/class-query output. Computing discarded patch outputs can inflate baseline FLOPs without improving the pooled representation.

Attention concentration, bounding-box overlap, and cosine diversity do not establish semantic part correspondence or absence of background shortcuts. Table 6 uses a classification-label-trained probe, so describing its localization as unsupervised is misleading.

strengths: The paper addresses a meaningful evaluation problem: global linear probes can understate the quality of representations learned through patch-level objectives. The unified treatment of attentive pooling methods is useful.
The reparameterization in Equations 7–10 is sound and provides concrete trainable-parameter savings. EP12 matches AIM12 at 75.1% accuracy while reducing parameters from 1.95M to 1.36M.

The experiments cover seven classification datasets and diverse pre-training families. Reported ImageNet gains over linear probing are substantial for MAE ViT-B (+7.9 points), SimMIM (+13.6), and DiT (+24.3).

The appendix provides substantial additional evidence, including dimensionality and query-count ablations, limited-data experiments, cross-dataset evaluation, retrieval, and LoRA combinations. These strengthen the practical case for the approach.
weaknesses: The methodological novelty is modest: the central mechanism is an exact reparameterization of existing learned-query attention. Consequently, the strongest potential contribution is the empirical study, whose comparisons must establish benefits beyond the already-known advantages of attentive over linear probing.

The computational-efficiency comparison lacks algebraically optimized baselines. Equation 7 also allows AIM to compute W_Kj^T q_j before multiplying by X; after training, these vectors can be folded exactly into effective queries. Thus, reduced trainable parameter count is established, but an intrinsic inference-compute advantage over optimized AIM is not. End-to-end runtime and peak-memory measurements are also absent, while the current protocol repeatedly executes the 17.58-GFLOP backbone.

Baseline optimization is insufficiently controlled for strong superiority claims. Appendix C.1 fixes the learning rate to 0.1 on ImageNet and Places365 across heterogeneous probing architectures. A common learning rate does not establish equally competitive optimization. No repeated-run uncertainty is reported, making small differences between attentive methods difficult to assess.

The low-parameter comparisons need compressed CLS/GAP and LoRA classifier baselines. Reducing EP's output dimension reduces classifier parameters substantially, whereas a full-dimensional baseline classifier imposes a higher parameter floor. Figure 15 usefully varies AIM's dimensions, but does not isolate classifier compression from attentive pooling in the broader LP and PEFT comparisons.

The attention analysis supports narrower conclusions than claimed. Replacing sharp attention with uniform attention introduces a larger perturbation than replacing an already diffuse map, confounding the entropy–importance relationship. Attention localization does not demonstrate avoidance of background shortcuts or improved robustness without appropriate interventions. Moreover, localization using a probe trained with ImageNet class labels should be described as weakly supervised, rather than unsupervised.

Reproducibility and reporting need improvement. The manuscript provides no code/configuration link and omits important details such as query initialization, weight decay, and DiT feature-extraction settings. Some statements also contradict the reported results: Table 9 shows MAE EP@10 substantially below LP@90, and Table 8 shows BEiTv2 retrieval declining on Cars despite claims of consistent improvement.
